property_summary: For any caller address, calling setOwner on the correct contract never changes owner unless the caller is the initial admin; the mutant that removed onlyAdmin allows non-admin callers to change owner, so there exist callers for which owner differs after the call.

For all callers (addresses) except the admin, calling setOwner does NOT change owner on the reference (only admin can set owner); the mutant removing onlyAdmin allows a non-admin caller to change owner, so there exists a caller and newOwner where owner changes after the call.

For every caller address and proposed new owner, only the original admin (deployer) can successfully change C.owner(); the mutant that removed the onlyAdmin modifier allows some non-admin caller to change owner, so there exist inputs (caller, newOwner) for which owner differs after the call.

For any caller address _owner provided to setOwner by the admin, the reference contract always updates the public owner state to that address (owner == _owner after the call); the mutant instead assigns admin = _owner so for some fuzzed _owner values the public owner remains unchanged, violating this property.

For any address _owner and when called by the admin, setOwner sets C.owner() equal to the supplied _owner; the mutant breaks this by always setting owner to address(0) so for some fuzzed _owner the post-call owner differs from the supplied value.

For every caller address A, when admin (the contract deployer) calls setOwner(A) the reference contract will set owner == A (call succeeds only for admin), whereas the mutant inverts onlyAdmin so admin cannot set owner but non-admins can, thus there exist caller addresses for which setOwner succeeds on the mutant but fails on the reference (and vice versa); we assert that if the caller is the admin then setOwner succeeds and owner equals the provided address.
For every call to setOwner made by the admin, the reference contract returns true upon successful completion; the mutant returns false for some inputs, breaking this return-value property.

For any caller who is the admin, calling setOwner(...) always returns true in the reference implementation; the mutant returns false when given address(0), thus violating this universal return-value rule for some input.

For any caller who is the admin, calling setOwner(x) returns true in the reference contract for every x that does not make the call revert (i.e. admin calls always succeed and return true); the mutant returns false when admin sets owner to address(0), violating this universal return-value rule for that input.

For all callers, calling setOwner(...) on the correct contract returns true only when the call completes (never returns false); the mutant removes the admin check and can cause a differing return value observable by non-admin callers (i.e., the reference always returns true on successful setOwner calls, the mutant can lead to a different return value for some caller), so the property is that any successful call to setOwner returns true — the mutant can produce a successful call that returns false for some fuzzed caller.

For any caller address A and any target owner O, if calling c.setOwner(O) completes (does not revert) then it returns true on the correct contract; the mutant that removes the onlyAdmin check can produce a completed call that returns false for some caller, so the property is that all successful setOwner calls return true.

For every caller and owner address, any non-reverting call to c.setOwner(owner) on the correct contract returns true; the mutant that changes onlyAdmin can allow a call that completes but yields a different return (false) for some caller, violating this rule.

For every caller and owner input, any non-reverting call to c.setOwner(owner) on the correct contract returns true; the mutant that removes the admin restriction can produce a non-reverting call that returns false for some caller, so the rule is violated for some fuzzed caller.

For every caller address and owner address, any non-reverting call to c.setOwner(owner) on the reference C returns true; the mutant that removes the admin check can allow a non-admin caller to call setOwner and produce a different observable result (a failing/false return) for some caller, breaking the rule.

For all callers, only the original admin (the deployer) can successfully call setOwner and change owner; the mutant that requires onlyOwner allows the current owner (not necessarily the admin) to call setOwner, violating this invariant for some inputs.

For every caller address x and candidate newOwner y, only the original deployer-admin can successfully invoke setOwner; the mutant that enforces onlyOwner instead allows the current owner (which may differ from the admin) to call setOwner and thus some callers other than the admin will succeed on the mutant but not on the reference.

For any caller address caller and target address newOwner, only the original deployer (admin) can successfully call setOwner on the reference contract; the mutant that uses onlyOwner instead allows a call by the current owner (which may be different from the admin) to succeed in cases where the owner != admin, so there exist inputs (a prior successful owner change by admin and then a setOwner call by that new owner) that the mutant accepts but the reference would reject.

Invariant: only the original deployer (admin) can call setOwner successfully no matter what prior state; the mutant instead allows the current owner to call setOwner, so after admin transfers ownership to some address A, A can call setOwner on the mutant but not on the reference.

For every caller address caller and candidate newOwner, only the original deployer (admin) can successfully call setOwner; the mutant that changes the modifier to onlyOwner allows the current owner (which can differ from admin after admin sets owner) to call setOwner, so there exist inputs where a non-admin owner can call setOwner on the mutant but not on the reference.

Only the admin (the deployer) can successfully call setOwner; the correct contract always only allows the original admin to change owner, whereas the mutant allows the current owner to call setOwner (so a non-admin owner can change owner), violating the rule for some fuzzed owner addresses.

For any admin caller and any address argument, calling setOwner(...) succeeds (does not revert) and updates the public owner to the provided address; the mutant makes setOwner always revert, breaking this property for some inputs.
